direction: Search structured constructions from scratch using the Hopf/Clifford-torus and quaternionic-lattice geometry of \(S^3\): parametrise points by Hopf coordinates, place them on a small number of Clifford tori with integer allocations summing to \(163\), initialise their angular coordinates from square, triangular, and twisted lattice patterns, and optimise torus positions, allocations, twists, and phases before releasing all coordinates to soft-max and LP polishing. In parallel, generate a large candidate pool from normalised Hurwitz/D\(_4\)-type rational quaternions and nearby lattice shells, select \(163\) candidates by greedy maximin insertion plus pairwise-swap improvement, polish the resulting code, and compare its contact graph with the incumbent; this seeks the regular or semi-regular structure absent from the current amorphous optimum.

idea: Delete large hub-centred connected clusters and reinsert them with taboo-weighted maximin optimisation to force contact-graph topology changes.
direction: Use large connected-cluster deletion and taboo reinsertion: choose clusters of \(8\)–\(20\) points consisting of a high-contact hub, its contact neighbours, and optionally one low-contact boundary point; freeze the remaining points, jointly reinsert the cluster by first solving a maximin hole-placement problem and then optimising only the cluster with a soft-max objective that temporarily penalises recreating any deleted old contact above \(\mathrm{maxcos}-10^{-4}\). Follow this with a short joint annealing phase and LP polish, retain results only when the final contact graph has substantial edit distance from the incumbent, and repeat over many hub-centred, low-contact-centred, and spatially localised clusters so that an entire jammed neighbourhood changes topology simultaneously rather than one or two points falling back into their former holes.

idea: Stressed-hub deletion with sub-target polishing plus greedy deep-hole reinsertion and topology-gated LP polish.
direction: Create rattlers by contact-stress surgery: load `best.npy`, identify the points with 8–9 contacts and the contacts with largest LP dual multipliers, delete $k\in\{6,10,14,18\}$ of the most stressed points, and re-polish the remaining $163-k$ points with annealed softmax followed by LP until their maximum is well below the full-code target. Sequentially reinsert points by sampling 20k uniform candidates on $S^3$, refining the best 20 holes by tangent descent against the fixed set, inserting the best hole, then locally relaxing the inserted point plus all neighbours with cosine $>0.75$; restart the greedy insertion with different orders when it stalls, keep several distinct reinsertions in an elite archive, and fully LP-polish only candidates whose contact graph differs measurably (e.g. Jaccard distance $>0.1$ from the incumbent), rather than accepting every near-tie back into the same basin.

idea: Force basin jumps with rigidity-guided LP breaks using floppy-mode drop sets at fixed large trust radii followed by repair and diversity retention.
direction: Force finite topology changes through the rigidity matrix: build the $490\times489$ rigidity matrix in per-point tangent coordinates for contacts at slack $<10^{-9}$, compute its smallest singular vectors, and combine this with the second tier of pairs at slack $<2\times10^{-4}$. Solve modified LPs in which a chosen subset of 15–40 high-dual contacts is explicitly allowed to increase by a prescribed amount (breaking them) while all retained and second-tier pairs must stay $\le t$, and the displacement is constrained to a large fixed trust radius such as $0.01$, $0.03$, or $0.06$ instead of being allowed to shrink to zero; try drop-sets clustered on one point, on one contact-graph community, and along low-singular-vector support, then repair with softmax/L-BFGS and standard LP polish, retaining results by both score and changed-contact count so that genuine bifurcations are not discarded for a tiny temporary increase in max cosine.

direction: Search symmetric orbit constructions that the amorphous incumbent cannot reach by perturbation: parametrise $R^4\simeq C^2$ and generate points as orbits under finite rotation groups acting as $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto(\omega z_1,\omega^m z_2)$ for cyclic orders $6,8,10,12$ and under quaternionic sign/permutation groups, choosing orbit sizes and a few special orbits on invariant circles to total exactly 163 points. Optimise only the orbit representatives and relative phases with the softmax objective under exact symmetry, then break the symmetry in stages—first allow orbit-wise radial/phase splitting, then release all points—and finish with LP polish; also try splicing two symmetry-generated halves related by a random quaternionic rotation, because a partially symmetric start imposes collective motions that can settle into a different, possibly lower, asymmetric optimum after release.

Random sequential packing to a trial cap threshold gives a de novo independent set with new topology, then annealed softmax plus L-BFGS and trust-region LP polish it to a local optimum.
direction: Build a de novo code as a large independent set in a spherical-cap graph, ignoring the incumbent except as a score target: generate a large low-discrepancy pool (50k–200k points from normalised Gaussians or Hopf coordinates on $S^3$), connect pool points whose cosine exceeds a trial threshold scanned around $0.854$–$0.8564$, and run greedy independent-set construction with randomised vertex weights plus 1-for-2 and 2-for-3 local swaps/backtracking until 163 mutually non-conflicting points are found or the pool is adaptively densified near promising holes. Take any 163-set found at or near the target threshold, however irregular, and only then apply annealed softmax, L-BFGS smoothing, and trust-region LP polish; repeat over many seeds and thresholds and archive polished outputs, since even a failed threshold slightly above the record can reveal a genuinely new packing topology inaccessible from the current jammed configuration.

idea: Below-record hinge feasibility continuation for decreasing tau with Riemannian L-BFGS and 20%-subset tangent kicks to allow active-pair topology changes, freezing feasible tau with LP polish.
direction: Replace minimax polishing by below-record feasibility continuation: for targets tau = 0.8559, 0.8555, 0.8550, 0.8545, minimise the hinge energy sum_{i<j} max(0, cos_ij - tau)^2 (plus 1e-3 times a softmax term to keep non-violating pairs separated) with Riemannian L-BFGS, starting each tau from the previous iterate plus a 0.03-0.08 rad tangent kick applied to a random 20% of points. This objective is allowed to let the current 480 contacts worsen temporarily as long as pairs cross below tau, unlike LP which forbids that, so it can change which pairs are active; whenever the hinge energy hits zero, freeze tau, run the standard LP polish, save the code, and step tau down, otherwise restart the tau step from best.npy with a different kick seed, spending at most ~150s total.

idea: Cyclic SO(4) orbit search with exact symmetric softmax gradients then staged symmetry breaking
direction: Search the symmetry-constrained manifold the record lacks, using 163 = 1 + 27*6: take the SO(4) cyclic action generated by block rotations through 2pi/27 in the (x1,x2) plane and 2pi*a/27 in the (x3,x4) plane for a in {5,8,11}, fix one point at a pole orbit representative, and parametrise the code by only 6 generic orbit representatives (24 free numbers) expanded to 162 points plus the special point. Optimise these few parameters with softmax L-BFGS (tau 0.003 -> 0.0003) for each a and for the alternative splittings 1+18*9 and 1+54*3, pick the best symmetric code (expected within a few 1e-3 of the record), then break symmetry gradually: add tangent noise of amplitude 0.005, 0.02, 0.05 in three successive full anneal + LP-polish stages, so the code can leave the symmetric submanifold into a nearby asymmetric basin whose contact graph is inherited from the group action rather than from the record.

idea: Stress-guided contiguous patch excision using an LP self-stress to find the most loaded contact and reinserting its whole BFS neighbourhood via maximin greedy holes plus staged patch-only/full annealing.
direction: Do stress-guided contiguous patch excision rather than deleting scattered hubs: build the active graph (slack < 1e-7), form its tangent Jacobian A (one row per active pair, projected gradients on S^3), solve the LP for a nonnegative self-stress lambda >= 0 with A^T lambda = 0, lambda != 0, then take the highest-lambda edge and delete its whole BFS neighbourhood of 15-25 points in the contact graph, creating one large hole instead of many pinholes. Freeze the remaining ~140 points, sample 20000 random unit vectors plus the removed points jittered by 0.15 rad, greedily place the deleted points at maximin holes against the frozen set (with the existing _refine_hole local relaxation), then unfreeze in two stages (patch-only softmax anneal at T 0.004->0.0004 for 1500 steps, then all-point anneal and LP polish), repeating for the top 4 stress edges with different patch radii 12/18/24.

idea: Contiguous patch excision around the highest self-stress contact, then frozen greedy maximin reinsertion with two-stage unfreezing.
direction: Do stress-guided contiguous patch excision rather than deleting scattered hubs: build the active graph (slack < 1e-7), form its tangent Jacobian A (one row per active pair, projected gradients on S^3), solve the LP for a nonnegative self-stress lambda >= 0 with A^T lambda = 0, lambda != 0, then take the highest-lambda edge and delete its whole BFS neighbourhood of 15-25 points in the contact graph, creating one large hole instead of many pinholes. Freeze the remaining ~140 points, sample 20000 random unit vectors plus the removed points jittered by 0.15 rad, greedily place the deleted points at maximin holes against the frozen set (with the existing _refine_hole local relaxation), then unfreeze in two stages (patch-only softmax anneal at T 0.004->0.0004 for 1500 steps, then all-point anneal and LP polish), repeating for the top 4 stress edges with different patch radii 12/18/24.

idea: Escape the isostatically jammed basin with hub-to-hole defect transplantation plus rigid-cap rotations and dual-scale softmax annealing followed by multi-temperature L-BFGS and LP freezing under basin-hopping.
